How to use the Google Sheets add-on

Work with your Mwakete contacts and SMS campaigns from inside a Google Sheet. The add-on never sends — you press Start on Mwakete.com and messages go out from your own phone and SIM. It also cannot delete contacts, change anyone’s consent, or see your phones or settings.

Set it up once

  1. Make a key. On Mwakete.com, open SMS → Settings → Google Sheets add-on. Give the key a name and press Make a key. Copy it now — it is shown only once. (Up to 5 keys per store.)
  2. Install it in your sheet. Open a Google Sheet, choose Extensions → Apps Script, then: replace Code.gs with the add-on’s Code.gs; add an HTML file named Sidebar and paste Sidebar.html; show and replace appsscript.json. Press Save and reload the sheet. (Full install steps are in the add-on README.)
  3. Connect. A Mwakete SMS menu appears → Open panel. Approve Google’s prompt (this sheet, its menu and panel, and talking to Mwakete.com only) and press Allow. Paste your key and press Connect. The key is kept in your Google account, not in the sheet.

Everyday use

Each of these is a button in the panel.

  • Get my contacts — fills a sheet called Mwakete contacts with everyone you have. It is replaced fresh each time.
  • Add contacts from a sheet — put people under recognised headers (see the table below), press Check rows to see how many are new, already in, repeated or have no usable number, then press Add these contacts. You can also add them to a group. Up to 2,000 rows at once.
  • Draft a campaign — write the message (you can use {first_name} and the like), choose who it goes to (a group, all your contacts, or the rows you selected in “Mwakete contacts”), press Check to see the recipient and SMS count, then Save draft. Open the link it gives you and press Start on Mwakete.com to send.
  • Campaign results — press Put results in a sheet to export a campaign’s sent, delivered and failed counts into a Results sheet.

Headers the sheet understands

Put these in row 1 when adding contacts. Any of the names shown will work.

FieldHeader names that work
First nameFirst name, Given name, Name
Last nameLast name, Surname
BusinessBusiness, Company, Store
PhonePhone, Mobile, Number, Tel
Island / VillageIsland, Village, Town
OtherEmail, Category / Type, Notes

Phone numbers follow the Kiribati rule: local numbers starting 730 or 630, with or without +686.

Good to know

  • Consent is deliberate. People are recorded as agreeing to promotions only if you tick the box and say how they agreed — the backend refuses a bare “yes”.
  • Keep the key safe. If a shared sheet leaks it, remove the key on SMS → Settings. The add-on then forgets it and asks for a new one.
  • Sending is on you. Drafts wait on Mwakete.com until you press Start; messages then send from your own SIM through the Mwakete SMS Android app, under your carrier’s terms.
  • It needs to be switched on. Contacts & SMS must be enabled for your store, and your store must be active.

Looking to sync stock or products instead? That is a different tool — Import & Sync on the dashboard — not this add-on.
